candidates.rationale: Drupal nav is logo + flat ul.menu with two nested submenus (Policyholders, Agents/Brokers) + a mobile .menu-icon. The boilerplate header covers every one of those: it marks any li containing a nested ul as .nav-drop, and injects its own hamburger below 900px.
Identical to the internal copy; no reason to re-vendor.
Could lay out nav items, but carries no nav semantics, keyboard handling or mobile toggle.

migration_note: IMPLEMENTED as a hard-coded block (blocks/header/header.js). Content is NOT authored in AEM yet, so the nav lives in a NAV_ITEMS array in the block rather than in a /nav fragment document; buildNav() emits the same DOM loadFragment() would have, so switching to fragment-driven content later is a one-function change. Covers all 6 top-level items and both 5-company submenus, with aria-current set from the URL. Logo extracted from the source site to icons/logo.webp. The Drupal data-drupal-link-system-path and is-active attributes are dropped.

candidates.rationale: A Drupal file-field widget wrapper ('Upload PDF files' label + field__items of file links) around the same authorial intent as pdf-link-list: a list of PDF downloads. The Drupal chrome is presentation scaffolding with no counterpart in EDS.
Only if the client wants file size/date columns alongside each document, which the source does not carry.

migration_note: No block authoring. Collapses to the same output as pdf-link-list, so both should share one transform rule. Link text is currently the raw filename (Primary_Press_Release_Final.pdf) - the transform should substitute human-readable titles, which the newsroom page already provides for the same two documents.

candidates.rationale: Source footer is two paragraphs - a pipe-separated link pair (Disclosures | Privacy Policy) and a copyright line. The boilerplate footer passes fragment content through untouched, which is exactly what this needs.

migration_note: IMPLEMENTED as a hard-coded block (blocks/footer/footer.js). Content is NOT authored in AEM yet, so the links and copyright live in the block rather than in a /footer fragment document; buildFooter() is a one-function swap when content lands. The link pair is rendered as a list with CSS-drawn dividers rather than literal '|' characters, and the external Privacy Policy link carries rel=noopener noreferrer. OPEN QUESTION: the copyright still reads 2014 as in the source - confirm the intended year with the client before publishing.
